definition: A small domesticated carnivorous mammal with soft fur, a short snout, and retractable claws.
fun_fact: Cats sleep between 12 and 16 hours a day — more than almost any other mammal. They are one of the most popular pets in the world.
hint: A furry pet that says 'meow' and loves chasing mice.

definition: A domesticated carnivorous mammal that has a long snout, an acute sense of smell, and is kept as a pet or for work.
fun_fact: Dogs have been domesticated for at least 15,000 years — longer than any other animal. Their sense of smell is 10,000 to 100,000 times stronger than humans.
hint: Man's best friend — loyal, barks, and loves fetch.

definition: The star around which the Earth orbits, providing light and heat to the solar system.
fun_fact: The Sun is so large that about 1.3 million Earths could fit inside it. Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
hint: It rises in the morning, sets at night, and gives us light and warmth.

definition: A diagrammatic representation of an area of land or sea showing physical features, cities, roads, etc.
fun_fact: The oldest known map is a Babylonian clay tablet from around 600 BCE. Today, Google Maps processes over 1 billion kilometres of directions every day.
hint: Travelers use this to find their way — it shows roads, cities, and borders.

definition: A container with a flat base and sides, typically square or rectangular and having a lid.
fun_fact: The corrugated cardboard box was invented in 1856 in England. Today, over 90% of all products in the United States are shipped in cardboard boxes.
hint: Amazon delivers things inside one of these — it's square and made of cardboard.

definition: To move at a speed faster than a walk, never having both or all feet on the ground at the same time.
fun_fact: The fastest human ever recorded is Usain Bolt, who reached 44.72 km/h in 2009. The word 'run' has over 645 meanings in English — the most of any word!
hint: What you do when you're late for the bus — faster than walking.

definition: A sweet baked food made from a mixture of flour, fat, eggs, sugar, and other ingredients.
fun_fact: The tradition of putting candles on birthday cakes comes from ancient Greece. People placed candles on cakes to make them glow like the moon as an offering to Artemis.
hint: You eat this on your birthday — often with candles on top.

definition: A limbless cold-blooded vertebrate animal with gills and fins living wholly in water.
fun_fact: There are over 33,000 species of fish — more than all other vertebrates combined. The whale shark is the largest fish, growing up to 12 metres long.
hint: It lives in water, has fins, and you might find it in an aquarium or on your dinner plate.

definition: Not closed or blocked; allowing access, passage, or a view.
fun_fact: The phrase 'open sesame' from Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves is one of the most famous magic words in literature. Sesame plants actually burst open with a popping sound when ripe!
hint: The opposite of closed — a door, a shop, or a window can be this.

definition: To engage in activity for enjoyment and recreation rather than a serious or practical purpose.
fun_fact: Play is so important for development that the United Nations recognizes it as a fundamental right of every child. Even adult animals like dolphins and crows are known to play for fun.
hint: What children do with toys — and what actors do on stage.

definition: To push oneself off a surface and into the air by using the muscles in one's legs and feet.
fun_fact: The highest human jump ever recorded is 2.45 metres by Javier Sotomayor in 1993. Fleas can jump 200 times their own body length — equivalent to a human jumping over a 35-story building.
hint: What a frog or a basketball player does — propelling upward off the ground.

definition: Water that falls from clouds as liquid droplets of various sizes.
fun_fact: A single raindrop falls at about 9 km/h. The smell of rain on dry earth has a special name: 'petrichor', coined by Australian scientists in 1964.
hint: It falls from the sky when clouds are grey — bring an umbrella!

definition: Of or at a low temperature; also a common illness causing a runny nose and sore throat.
fun_fact: You don't catch a cold from being cold — you catch it from a virus. However, cold air can dry out nasal passages, making it slightly easier for viruses to enter.
hint: The opposite of hot — also the name of a common winter illness.

definition: Moving or capable of moving at high speed; also to abstain from eating for a period of time.
fun_fact: The cheetah is the fastest land animal at 112 km/h. Interestingly, 'fast' meaning 'quick' and 'fast' meaning 'to not eat' are completely unrelated words — they just happen to look the same!
hint: Usain Bolt is this on a track — also what you do during Ramadan.

definition: Producing or capable of producing much noise; easily audible.
fun_fact: The loudest sound ever recorded was the 1883 eruption of Krakatoa — heard 4,800 kilometres away in Australia. A rocket launch can reach 180 decibels, enough to cause instant hearing damage.
hint: A rock concert or a thunderstorm is this — the opposite of quiet.

definition: A series of thoughts, images, and sensations occurring in a person's mind during sleep; also a cherished ambition.
fun_fact: You forget 90% of your dreams within 10 minutes of waking up. Blind people who were born sighted can see in their dreams, but those born blind experience dreams through their other senses.
hint: What happens in your mind while you sleep — or your biggest wish for the future.

definition: Not previously known or used; new or different. Also: recently made or obtained; not stale.
fun_fact: The phrase 'fresh as a daisy' comes from the fact that daisies close at night and reopen in the morning — always appearing new and bright. The word comes from Old English 'fersc', meaning not salt (of water).
hint: A baker's bread straight from the oven is this — new and not stale.

definition: Ready to face and endure danger or pain; showing courage.
fun_fact: The word 'brave' comes from Italian 'bravo' (wild, savage) and Spanish 'bravo' (courageous). Interestingly, 'bravo' shouted at performers originally meant they were 'savagely good' — dangerously talented!
hint: A firefighter running into a burning building is being this — the opposite of cowardly.

definition: A hard, brittle, typically transparent substance made by fusing sand with soda and lime.
fun_fact: Glass is technically a supercooled liquid, not a solid — it flows extremely slowly over centuries. Ancient glass windows are thicker at the bottom because glassblowers placed them that way, not because of 'flowing'.
hint: Windows are made of this — also what you drink water from.

definition: A large plant-eating domesticated mammal with solid hoofs and a flowing mane and tail, used for riding and to carry loads.
fun_fact: Horses can sleep both standing up and lying down. They have the largest eyes of any land mammal, and can see nearly 360 degrees around them.
hint: Cowboys ride this animal — it has a mane, hooves, and says 'neigh'.

definition: To mix and combine substances so that they become an integrated whole.
fun_fact: The word 'blend' gave us 'blender', which was invented in 1922. Smoothies became popular in the 1960s in health food stores in California — long before Instagram made them famous.
hint: What you do with ingredients in a smoothie maker — mix them together completely.

definition: To seize and hold firmly; also to understand a concept fully.
fun_fact: Babies are born with a 'palmar grasp reflex' — they instinctively grip anything placed in their palm. This reflex disappears around 6 months but the word 'grasp' for understanding persisted into adult vocabulary.
hint: You can physically do this to a rope — or mentally do this to a new idea.

definition: To grow or develop well and vigorously; to be successful, healthy, or prosperous.
fun_fact: Plants, businesses, and people can all 'thrive'. Interestingly, 'thrive' comes from Old Norse 'þrífast', meaning to grasp or seize — suggesting success comes from actively grabbing opportunities!
hint: What a plant does when you give it water and sunlight — it doesn't just survive, it does this.

definition: Moving or handling things in an awkward way; difficult to handle or use.
fun_fact: The word comes from a Scandinavian root meaning 'benumbed with cold' — when your hands are frozen, you naturally drop things! In British slang, someone very clumsy might be called a 'butterfingers'.
hint: Someone who always drops things and bumps into furniture is often described as this.

definition: To disappear suddenly and completely, often in a way that is difficult to explain.
fun_fact: Magicians 'vanish' objects during tricks. The word comes from Old French 'evanir', related to Latin 'evanescere' — the same root as 'evanescent', meaning something fleeting and short-lived.
hint: What a magician makes a rabbit do — or what your motivation does on a Monday morning.

definition: To stay in a place longer than necessary, typically because of a reluctance to leave.
fun_fact: Often used to describe a pleasant smell or feeling that stays around: 'The smell of fresh bread lingered in the kitchen.'
hint: What you do when you don't want to leave a place — you hang around.

definition: To understand a difficult problem or situation after much thought. Also a unit of depth equal to 6 feet, used in measuring water.
fun_fact: Originally a nautical term for measuring sea depth — sailors would use their outstretched arms (a 'fathom') to measure rope. Now it's common to say 'I can't fathom it!' meaning you can't understand something.
hint: A sailor might measure depth with this word — or a philosopher might struggle to do this with a mystery.

definition: Calm, peaceful, and untroubled; tranquil.
fun_fact: From Latin 'serenus' (clear, cloudless sky). A serene lake reflects the sky perfectly — hence the visual image of calm. 'Serenity Now!' became famous in the TV show Seinfeld, though it was used as a joke about forced calmness.
hint: A mountain lake at dawn, perfectly still and peaceful — the scene is this.

definition: To think about something carefully and for a long time before making a decision or reaching a conclusion.
fun_fact: From Latin 'ponderare', meaning to weigh. When you ponder something, you're mentally 'weighing' the options. A similar origin gave us 'ponderous' (heavy) and even 'pound' (unit of weight)!
hint: A philosopher sitting quietly with a furrowed brow is doing this — deep thinking.

definition: Having or showing sharp powers of judgment; clever in practical matters, especially in business.
fun_fact: Originally meant 'wicked' or 'evil' in Middle English (from 'shrew', a scolding person). Over centuries, it shifted to mean 'sharp-minded'. Shakespeare used it to mean cunning in 'The Taming of the Shrew'!
hint: A great negotiator or businessperson is often described as this — sharp and clever.

definition: To complain about something in a bad-tempered way; also the low rumbling sound of thunder.
fun_fact: Onomatopoeic in origin — the word itself sounds like a low, discontented murmur. In Tolkien's 'The Hobbit', the dragon Smaug's roar is sometimes described with similar sounds. Grumpy, grumble, growl — all share that unhappy 'gr' sound!
hint: What someone does when they're unhappy but not angry enough to shout — they mutter and complain quietly.

definition: Wildly excited or uncontrolled because of fear, worry, or the urgency of a situation.
fun_fact: From Greek 'phrenitis' (inflammation of the brain), via Latin. The same root gives us 'frenzy'. When someone is frantic, their thoughts are racing like a 'frenzied' mind — an ancient medical concept made into an emotion word!
hint: How parents feel when they can't find their child in a supermarket — a panicked, frenzied feeling.

definition: A stupid or careless mistake, often made due to lack of attention or poor judgment.
fun_fact: In chess, a 'blunder' is one of the worst moves a player can make, often losing a major piece. Chess engines will call your move a blunder if it costs you significant advantage!
hint: Think of a clumsy person tripping and knocking everything over — that's a big one of these.

definition: To become dry and shriveled; to lose vitality, freshness, or importance; to cause to feel embarrassed.
fun_fact: A 'withering look' is a famously powerful expression — a glance so cold and disapproving it makes you feel like a plant dying in the sun. Shakespeare used 'wither' dramatically in his plays to describe characters losing hope.
hint: What flowers do when they haven't had water — they droop and shrink.

definition: Gentle and kind; not harmful in effect. In medicine, a benign tumor is not cancerous.
fun_fact: Opposite of 'malign' (harmful). Both share the Latin root — 'bene' (good) vs 'male' (bad). You'll often hear doctors say 'the tumor is benign' as very good news. A benign dictator? That's an oxymoron!
hint: A kind, gentle person or a non-dangerous medical condition can both be called this.

definition: Lasting for a very short time; transitory by nature.
fun_fact: From Greek 'ephemeros' — 'epi' (on) + 'hemera' (day), meaning 'lasting only a day'. The mayfly lives only 24 hours as an adult, making it the ultimate symbol of the ephemeral in nature.
hint: Cherry blossoms that fall after just a few days are the perfect symbol of this quality — beautiful but brief.

definition: The state of being unaware or unconscious of what is happening; the state of being forgotten, especially by the public.
fun_fact: From Latin 'oblivisci' (to forget). The River Lethe in Greek mythology was the river of forgetfulness — drinking from it caused total oblivion of one's past life. The video game 'The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion' named itself after this concept.
hint: A celebrity who was once famous but now is completely forgotten has slipped into this state.

definition: Tending to keep a firm hold of something; clinging or adhering strongly; not readily relinquishing a position or principle.
fun_fact: From Latin 'tenax' (holding fast), related to 'tenere' (to hold). The band 'Tenacious D' chose their name deliberately — Jack Black wanted a name that conveyed unstoppable rock energy. 'D' stands for 'Dick' or simply the musical note.
hint: A bulldog that refuses to let go of a bone is the classic image of this quality — stubborn and persistent.

definition: Using very few words; brief and concise in speech or expression.
fun_fact: From the Laconians (Spartans of ancient Laconia), famous for extremely brief, blunt speech. When Philip of Macedon threatened 'If I enter Laconia, I will raze Sparta to the ground', the Spartans replied with just one word: 'If'.
hint: A Spartan warrior's answer consisted of just one word — that style of speaking is described as this.

definition: The occurrence and development of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.
fun_fact: Coined by Horace Walpole in 1754, based on a Persian fairy tale 'The Three Princes of Serendip' (old name for Sri Lanka) who made fortunate discoveries by accident. The sticky note, penicillin, and microwave oven were all serendipitous inventions.
hint: Finding a 20-euro note in a coat you haven't worn in a year — that's pure this.

definition: Experienced in the imagination through the feelings or actions of another person.
fun_fact: From Latin 'vicarius' (substitute). When you feel nervous watching someone else give a speech, or excited watching a sports game, that's vicarious emotion. Binge-watching TV shows is essentially organized vicarious living.
hint: When you experience excitement by watching someone else's adventure — you feel it through them, not yourself.

definition: To use ambiguous or unclear language so as to conceal the truth or avoid commitment.
fun_fact: From Latin 'aequivocus' (of equal voice). Politicians are famous for equivocating — saying something that technically isn't a lie but deliberately misleads. Shakespeare's Porter in Macbeth delivers a famous speech about equivocation.
hint: A politician who gives a 10-minute answer that never actually answers the question is doing this.

definition: Having a pleasant, smooth, rich, flowing sound; sweet or musical; pleasant to hear.
fun_fact: From Latin 'mel' (honey) + 'fluere' (to flow) — literally 'flowing with honey'. Morgan Freeman's voice is often described as mellifluous. The word itself, when spoken aloud, demonstrates its own meaning.
hint: Morgan Freeman's voice, a cello played beautifully, or a mountain stream — all could be described with this word meaning 'honey-flowing'.

definition: To render obscure, unclear, or unintelligible; to bewilder or confuse someone.
fun_fact: From Latin 'ob' (over) + 'fuscare' (to darken). Lawyers and bureaucrats are sometimes accused of obfuscating simple truths with complex jargon. In computer science, 'obfuscated code' is deliberately written to be unreadable.
hint: A deliberately confusing legal contract full of impossible jargon is designed to do this — to cloud understanding.

definition: A person who acts obsequiously toward someone important in order to gain advantage; a flatterer or yes-man.
fun_fact: From Greek 'sykophantes' (informer). Originally meant someone who brought accusations about illegal fig exports in ancient Athens — it evolved to mean a false accuser, then a flatterer. Today's office 'yes-man' has ancient Greek roots.
hint: The employee who laughs at every one of the boss's jokes even when they're terrible — purely to get a promotion.

definition: Tending to talk a great deal; garrulous and talkative, often to an excessive degree.
fun_fact: From Latin 'loquax', from 'loqui' (to talk). Its opposite is 'laconic'. Interestingly, 'eloquent' (speaking beautifully) shares the same Latin root 'loqui' — both are about talking, but one implies too much, the other implies excellence.
hint: Your friend who never stops talking at dinner, covering 15 topics before the appetizer arrives — they are this.

definition: The region of the atmosphere and outer space seen from the earth.
fun_fact: The sky appears blue because of 'Rayleigh scattering'—Earth's atmosphere scatters shorter blue wavelengths more than longer red ones.
hint: Look up during the day to see it blue, or at night to see stars.

definition: Frozen water, a brittle transparent crystalline solid.
fun_fact: Ice is actually less dense than liquid water, which is why ice cubes float in your drink. Most other substances sink when they freeze!
hint: You put this in your drink to make it cold, or skate on it in winter.

definition: A written or printed work consisting of pages glued or sewn together along one side and bound in covers.
fun_fact: The fear of running out of reading material is called 'abibliophobia'. The world's best-selling book is the Bible, followed by Don Quixote.
hint: You read this to learn a story or information; it has many pages.

definition: Combustion or burning, in which substances combine chemically with oxygen from the air and typically give out bright light, heat, and smoke.
fun_fact: Fire doesn't have a shadow because it is a source of light itself. If you shine a brighter light through a flame, you might see a faint shadow of the soot!
hint: It's hot, it glows orange, and you use it to cook or stay warm.

definition: An organ of soft nervous tissue contained in the skull of vertebrates, functioning as the coordinating center of sensation and intellectual and nervous activity.
fun_fact: Your brain generates about 12-25 watts of electricity—enough to power a low-wattage LED light bulb!
hint: The organ inside your head that you use to think and solve puzzles.

definition: A violent disturbance of the atmosphere with strong winds and usually rain, thunder, lightning, or snow.
fun_fact: At any given moment, there are about 2,000 thunderstorms happening on Earth. Jupiter has a storm called the Great Red Spot that has lasted for over 300 years.
hint: When the weather gets very angry with loud thunder and bright lightning.

definition: A game, toy, or problem designed to test ingenuity or knowledge.
fun_fact: The first jigsaw puzzle was created around 1760 by a mapmaker who pasted a map onto wood and cut out the countries to help children learn geography.
hint: A game where you have to put pieces together or solve a difficult problem.

definition: An apparition of a dead person which is believed to appear or become manifest to the living.
fun_fact: The belief in ghosts is one of the most common paranormal beliefs in the world, appearing in almost every culture's folklore since ancient times.
hint: A spooky spirit that says 'Boo!' and is often depicted wearing a white sheet.

definition: An act of traveling from one place to another.
fun_fact: The word comes from the Old French 'journée', which meant the distance one could travel in a single day.
hint: A long trip to a far-off place.

definition: Speak very softly using one's breath rather than one's throat, especially for the sake of secrecy.
fun_fact: When you whisper, your vocal cords don't vibrate. This is why it's hard to tell the difference between 'p' and 'b' sounds in a whisper!
hint: To talk very quietly so that other people cannot hear you.

definition: Full of energy and enthusiasm; or (of color) bright and striking.
fun_fact: The human eye can see more shades of green than any other color because our ancestors needed to distinguish between different types of vegetation.
hint: A city full of life or a very bright, bold color can be described as this.

definition: No longer produced or used; out of date.
fun_fact: Floppy disks and VHS tapes are classic examples of technology that became obsolete almost overnight once CDs and streaming arrived.
hint: Something that is old-fashioned and no longer useful, like a typewriter.

definition: The state or situation of being alone.
fun_fact: There is a big difference between 'loneliness' (negative) and 'solitude' (positive). Many artists and writers seek solitude to spark their creativity.
hint: Being alone by choice, often to find peace or think clearly.

definition: Fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing.
fun_fact: The root 'loqu' comes from Latin 'loqui', meaning 'to speak'. It's the same root found in 'loquacious' (talking too much)!
hint: Someone who speaks very beautifully and can easily convince others with their words.

definition: Very complicated or detailed.
fun_fact: The internal mechanisms of a mechanical watch are among the most intricate objects ever designed by humans, with hundreds of tiny moving parts.
hint: A pattern or a plan that has many small, complex details.

definition: Able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions.
fun_fact: The 'Tardigrade' (or water bear) is the most resilient creature on Earth; it can survive in outer space, boiling water, and deep-sea pressure.
hint: Someone who bounces back quickly after a failure or a hard time.

definition: A typical example or pattern of something; a model.
fun_fact: The phrase 'paradigm shift' was made popular by Thomas Kuhn to describe a fundamental change in basic concepts of a scientific discipline.
hint: A standard way of thinking about or doing something; a perfect model.

definition: A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds.
fun_fact: From Greek 'kakos' (bad) + 'phone' (sound). It's the literal opposite of 'euphony' (beautiful sound).
hint: The sound of an orchestra tuning their instruments all at once—loud and unmusical.

definition: The expression or application of human creative skill and imagination.
fun_fact: Art used to be an Olympic event! Between 1912 and 1948, medals were awarded for painting, sculpture, architecture, and music.
hint: Paintings in a museum or drawings in your notebook are examples of this.

definition: A small piece of shaped metal with incisions which is inserted into a lock and turned to open or close it.
fun_fact: The oldest known locks and keys were found in the ruins of Nineveh and are over 4,000 years old.
hint: You need this to unlock your front door or start some cars.

definition: The perceptible natural movement of the air, especially in the form of a current of air blowing from a particular direction.
fun_fact: The fastest wind speed ever recorded on Earth (not in a tornado) was 408 km/h on Barrow Island, Australia.
hint: You can't see it, but you can feel it blowing your hair or moving the trees.

definition: A sound or series of sounds caused by the reflection of sound waves from a surface back to the listener.
fun_fact: The word comes from Greek mythology—Echo was a nymph who could only repeat the last words spoken to her.
hint: When you shout in a cave and your voice comes back to you.

definition: A very large expanse of sea, in particular each of the main areas into which the sea is divided geographically.
fun_fact: We have explored less than 5% of the Earth's oceans. There are more historic artifacts under the sea than in all the world's museums combined!
hint: The Atlantic or the Pacific; it's filled with salt water and whales.

definition: A fitted covering for the hand with a separate sheath for each finger and the thumb.
fun_fact: In the Middle Ages, throwing down a glove (a gauntlet) was a way of challenging someone to a duel.
hint: You wear these on your hands when it's freezing cold outside.

definition: A structure carrying a road, path, railroad, or canal across an obstacle.
fun_fact: The Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge in China is the longest in the world, stretching over 164 kilometers!
hint: A structure that lets you cross over a river or a busy highway.

definition: To light or set on fire; to inspire a feeling or emotion.
fun_fact: The popular e-reader was named 'Kindle' to suggest the idea of lighting a fire in the mind through reading.
hint: A verb for starting a fire, or starting a feeling of interest.

definition: Attractively unusual or old-fashioned.
fun_fact: Originally, 'quaint' meant 'wise' or 'knowing'. Over time, it shifted to mean 'cleverly made', then finally 'old-fashioned and charming'.
hint: A small, cute old village with stone houses would be described as this.

definition: The time at which something is most powerful or successful; the point in the sky directly above an observer.
fun_fact: The opposite of 'zenith' is 'nadir'—the lowest point. Both terms come from Arabic astronomy.
hint: The very highest point of a career or the sun's position at noon.

definition: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past.
fun_fact: Nostalgia was once considered a medical disease! In the 17th century, Swiss doctors thought it was a physical heart condition felt by soldiers.
hint: The feeling you get when you look at old childhood photos or hear a song from your youth.

definition: Open to more than one interpretation; having a double meaning.
fun_fact: The word comes from Latin 'ambigere', meaning 'to wander about'—fitting for a word that doesn't have a straight answer!
hint: When a sentence or a sign isn't clear and could mean two different things.

definition: Fond of company; sociable.
fun_fact: From the Latin 'grex', meaning 'flock'. A gregarious person is literally someone who likes to be part of the flock/group.
hint: A person who is very social and loves being surrounded by people.

definition: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
fun_fact: The word originally meant 'fearful' (from Latin 'metus'). It implied someone was so afraid of making a mistake they became extremely careful.
hint: Someone who cleans every tiny corner or checks their work ten times is this.

definition: A pleasant smell that frequently accompanies the first rain after a long period of warm, dry weather.
fun_fact: The word was created by scientists in 1964. It comes from 'petra' (stone) and 'ichor' (the fluid that flows in the veins of Greek gods).
hint: That wonderful earthy smell in the air right after a summer rainstorm.

definition: A female parent; the person who cares for a child.
fun_fact: Many languages have short, similar words for mother, like 'mama' or 'mom'.
hint: The person who often tucks you in at night.

definition: A male parent; someone who often helps and protects the family.
fun_fact: The word 'dad' is used in many cultures as an affectionate name for father.
hint: The person who might teach you to ride a bike.

definition: An object for children to play with.
fun_fact: The oldest known toys include small carved animals and dolls found in ancient tombs.
hint: Kids play with this to have fun.

definition: A white liquid produced by mammals used as food.
fun_fact: Humans have been drinking milk from other animals for thousands of years.
hint: You pour this on cereal in the morning.

definition: A covering for the foot, typically made of leather or fabric.
fun_fact: Shoes were once a sign of social status in many cultures.
hint: You put this on before leaving the house.

definition: A round fruit with sweet or tart flesh and a thin skin.
fun_fact: There are over 7,500 varieties of apples grown worldwide.
hint: A crunchy fruit often red or green.

definition: A tool used for writing with ink.
fun_fact: The ballpoint pen was patented in the 20th century and revolutionized writing.
hint: You use this to sign a paper.

definition: A small open container used for drinking.
fun_fact: Cups have been used since ancient times for ceremonies and daily life.
hint: You drink tea or coffee from this.

definition: A flexible container used to carry items.
fun_fact: Bags have been made from leather, cloth, and synthetic materials across history.
hint: You put your lunch or books inside this.

definition: A piece of furniture for sleeping or resting.
fun_fact: Beds have evolved from simple mats to complex designs with springs and mattresses.
hint: You sleep on this at night.

definition: A device that moves air to cool a space or person.
fun_fact: Handheld fans were used for centuries before electric fans existed.
hint: It blows air to make you feel cooler.

definition: A small rodent with a long tail, often found near humans.
fun_fact: Rats are highly adaptable and can live in many environments.
hint: A small animal that scurries and has a long tail.

definition: A farm animal raised for meat and other products.
fun_fact: Pigs are intelligent and can be trained to perform tasks.
hint: A farm animal that likes mud and says 'oink'.

definition: An insect that makes honey and pollinates flowers.
fun_fact: Bees are responsible for pollinating a large portion of the world’s crops.
hint: A small flying insect that makes honey.

definition: A short sleep taken during the day.
fun_fact: Short naps can improve mood and alertness without affecting nighttime sleep.
hint: A quick sleep after lunch.

definition: To rest with the body supported by the buttocks on a seat.
fun_fact: Sitting is a basic human posture used for eating, working, and resting.
hint: What you do on a chair.

definition: To consume food for nourishment.
fun_fact: Eating habits vary widely across cultures and climates.
hint: What you do at mealtimes.

definition: To move at a regular pace by lifting and setting down each foot in turn.
fun_fact: Walking is one of the simplest and healthiest forms of exercise.
hint: Move on foot at a steady pace.

definition: A facial expression showing happiness or friendliness.
fun_fact: Smiling can be contagious and improve both your mood and others'.
hint: What you do when you are happy.

definition: A staple food made from flour and water, usually baked.
fun_fact: Bread is one of the oldest prepared foods, with evidence dating back thousands of years.
hint: You slice this for toast.

definition: A visible mass of condensed water vapor floating in the atmosphere.
fun_fact: Clouds are classified into types like cumulus and stratus based on shape and altitude.
hint: White shapes you see in the sky.

definition: A flat dish from which food is eaten or served.
fun_fact: Plates were once luxury items made from precious metals for the wealthy.
hint: You put your dinner on this.

definition: Having the taste of sugar or honey; pleasant and delightful.
fun_fact: Sweet flavors often signal energy-rich foods to humans and animals.
hint: Candy and cake taste like this.

definition: A tool with bristles used for cleaning or painting.
fun_fact: Brushes have been used for art and hygiene for thousands of years.
hint: You use this to clean your teeth or paint a picture.

definition: Free from dirt, marks, or impurities.
fun_fact: Cleaning habits and rituals differ widely across cultures and history.
hint: What you do to make something tidy.

definition: Of limited size; not large.
fun_fact: Perception of size can change depending on context and comparison.
hint: The opposite of big.

definition: Feeling or showing pleasure or contentment.
fun_fact: Smiling and social connection are linked to increased happiness.
hint: Feeling good and joyful.
